personality_one_liner: A warm, high-contrast, chunky, and highly accessible interface that feels friendly and intuitive for first-time online buyers in rural India.

spacing.rule: Generous spacing to accommodate large tap targets (minimum 48x48pt for accessibility). Avoid dense layouts; use clear separation between modules.

dont's: No glassmorphism for this app. We need high contrast, solid surfaces, and maximum readability for the rural audience, falling back to 'solid surfaceSecondary' on elevated elements.

screens.name: Customer Home
screens.purpose: A highly readable, accessible storefront where users can toggle between Food and Daily Essentials, and browse prominent category cards.

states.empty: Illustration of a basket with 'Nothing here yet!' and a 'Refresh' button.
states.error: Readable error text ('Something went wrong') with a large 'Retry' button.

screens.layout: Sticky top bar containing Address/Location and a prominent Section Switcher (Food vs Daily Essentials vs Others). Below it, a large Search Bar (supporting Hindi keywords). Next, a bold 'Categories' grid (2-column, chunky cards with real imagery). Product rows follow (large image, clear MRP strike-through, selling price, and a very prominent 'Add to Cart' pill button). A sticky cart summary floating above the bottom tab bar when items are in cart.

screens.name: Customer Cart & Checkout
screens.purpose: A friction-free checkout flow summarizing items, clearly showing savings, and prioritizing Cash on Delivery.

states.empty: Empty basket illustration with text 'Your cart is empty. Let's add something!'

screens.layout: List of cart items with large (+) and (-) quantity steppers. Below the list, a clear bill details card highlighting 'Total Savings' in success color. A section for 'Apply Coupon'. The bottom has a fixed container with the Total Amount and a massive 'Place Order (COD)' button.

screens.name: Order Tracking
screens.purpose: Keeps the user informed with a visual vertical stepper of their order status.
screens.layout: Top map/illustration area showing delivery zones, followed by a bold vertical stepper (Order Placed -> Preparing -> Out for Delivery -> Delivered). Below the stepper, delivery partner details (name, call button) and order summary. Large 'Reorder' button at the bottom.

screens.name: Delivery Partner Dashboard
screens.purpose: A utility-first interface for partners to toggle online status, view earnings, and manage active deliveries.

states.empty: Illustration showing 'No active deliveries right now.'

screens.layout: Sticky top header with a massive Online/Offline toggle switch. Below it, today's earnings and completed trips in big bold numbers. The main body lists active delivery requests (Pickup/Drop locations, earnings, and a huge 'Accept' swipe/button). Details view includes OTP confirmation.

screens.name: Admin Dashboard
screens.purpose: Overview of business metrics, order management, and inventory for store operators.
screens.layout: Scrollable dashboard with 2-column chunky stat cards (Total Orders, Revenue, Active Partners). Below are quick access rows to 'Manage Inventory', 'Manage Orders', and 'Coupons'. Use prominent dividers and standard list items.

instructions_to_main_agent: Follow '4 Tactile / Playful LIGHT' strictly. Use chunky, highly readable UI with strong foreground/background contrast.
Accessibility is the top priority for this rural target audience: Touch targets must be at least 48x48pt. Font sizes are scaled up (base text is 16pt instead of standard 14pt).
Absolutely NO blue, indigo, or purple. Use the defined Saffron / Deep Orange (#E65100) brand color.
Ensure the sticky primary CTAs (like 'Place Order' or 'Add to Cart') are massive, fixed at the bottom of the screen (respecting safe areas), and unmissable.
Avoid glassmorphism. Use solid elevated surfaces (surfaceSecondary with shadow tier 2) for clarity on lower-end Android devices common in rural areas.
The Customer Home screen must feature the Section Switcher (Food vs Daily Essentials vs Others) prominently near the top.
Product cards must clearly show MRP with a strike-through next to the selling price and an unmistakable 'Add' pill button.
